pairs.question: Quando dabitur hostis, quando in manus veniet?
pairs.derivation: Within Agricola's battle speech he quotes the soldiers' own words verbatim, framed by 'fortissimi cuiusque voces audiebam:' (speech tag dropped as framing). The quoted utterance is a genuine interrogative; the editorial supplement '[veniet]' has its brackets stripped, words kept, and the question mark normalized. Agricola answers it immediately with 'Veniunt' ('they are coming'). The answer stops after 'Veniunt, e latebris suis extrusi.' — the direct answer to whether/when the enemy will come — cutting before 'et vota virtusque in aperto, omniaque prona victoribus atque eadem victis adversa,' where the speaker turns from answering to general elaboration on the battle's prospects. (The first full stop falls after 'adversa', but the contiguous answering span ends at 'extrusi'.)
